paragraphs: Direct assessment: If you are willing to respond steadily under pressure and in crises, document work under assessment and confidentiality standards, and help others, this direction is worth exploring further. The safe trial uses only entirely fictional service cases, with no real client information or restricted data.

Observable signals: Can you follow assessment and risk-screening processes, strictly maintain confidentiality and recordkeeping standards, and escalate immediately when safety risks arise? Personality labels cannot determine fit or eligibility.

Conditions supporting fit: Willingness to handle emotional demands and crisis situations over the long term, work steadily under supervision and standards, and keep learning. Reasons for caution: If high emotional demands and safety responsibilities are difficult to tolerate, or confidentiality requirements feel uncomfortable, first compare adjacent directions such as counseling or case management.

Safe work sample (entirely fictional service case): For a fictional referral case, spend 60 minutes writing a needs and risk assessment, service plan objectives, intervention and documentation points, confidentiality and escalation situations, and matters requiring confirmation by qualified people or the institution. Use no real client information or restricted data.

entries: Assessment and planning: Conduct psychosocial assessments and risk screening and develop reviewable service plans.

paragraphs: Mental health and substance abuse social workers correspond to O*NET 21-1023.00. They assess and help people with mental, emotional, or substance use problems, including alcohol, tobacco, and other drugs. Work may include individual and group therapy, crisis intervention, case management, client advocacy, prevention, and education. This page does not equate services with diagnostic or compulsory intervention authority.

Work context (O*NET work-context survey, 1–5 scale): Characterized by intensive interpersonal contact, emotional demands, and crisis situations, requiring documentation under confidentiality and safety standards. Specific context values follow the O*NET work-context survey.

Abilities and work approach: Fundamentals of psychosocial assessment, intervention, and crisis response; strict confidentiality and recordkeeping; and escalation through procedures when safety risks arise.

Research inputs: Official O*NET 21-1023.00 description, tasks, work context, interest code SI, and Job Zone Five, plus BLS 2025 wages and 2024–2034 employment projections for this occupation. These do not establish mainland Chinese qualifications, wages, or employment scope.
Work subjects and inputs: Clients with mental health or substance use problems, their families and support networks, referral sources, and community resources.
Inspectable outputs: Assessments and service plans, intervention and case management records, crisis response and referral records, and follow-up and handover records.
Boundary: This page covers assessment, intervention, and case management under O*NET 21-1023.00, excluding clinical diagnostic authority, prescribing, or compulsory intervention powers.

Adjacent roles are for comparing directions only: This occupation centers on assessment, intervention, and case management; clinical and counseling psychologists emphasize psychological assessment and treatment; substance abuse counselors emphasize addiction counseling; marriage and family therapists emphasize family systems; and mental health counselors emphasize counseling and support. Qualifications and licenses are not interchangeable.
When comparing roles, check each point: Who assesses, who treats, who may intervene in crises, and who bears legal responsibility? Similar titles do not establish equivalent duties or authority.

Difference from clinical and counseling psychologists: Psychologists typically require doctoral education and licensure and may provide psychological assessment and treatment. Verify this occupation's licensure and scope by jurisdiction.
Difference from substance abuse counselors: They focus on addiction counseling; this occupation has a broader scope including psychosocial assessment and case management.
Difference from mental health counselors: Scopes overlap; verify specific authorization, supervision, and legal responsibilities by jurisdiction and license.

description.text: Mental health and substance abuse social workers (O*NET 21-1023.00) assess and help people with mental health or substance use problems, providing case management, crisis intervention, and prevention education. U.S. BLS median annual pay was $60,280 in 2025, with approximately 136,800 employed in 2024. Includes work context, risks, and entry paths.
